title: double free of a tuple the write path had already freed
live_proof: inspection at the 17.0 pin: writetup_heap (src/backend/utils/sort/tuplestore.c:1500) frees the tuple at :1516-1517, after the BufFileWrite calls at :1511-1514 that can throw; dumptuples:1222 calls it in a loop and clears memtupdeleted/memtupcount only afterwards at :1225-1226; tuplestore_clear:428-432 then walks the same range with GetMemoryChunkSpace and pfree. The pre-fix shape is present.
object: a tuple chunk still listed in memtuples[]
lifetime_ender: writetup_heap frees each tuple as it writes it; a throw leaves the already-freed entries inside memtupdeleted..memtupcount for the cleanup walk to free again
shape: double free through a stale array entry

spatial.negative_control: HELD. The same program with PG_NEGATIVE_CONTROL, which replaces the one invalid access with a valid one, completes on this arm with no fault (results/20261010-control). The detection therefore depends on the defect and not on the allocation pattern.

sublet.oracle: fault anywhere; the stale access is the second pfree, so there is no read probe
sublet.negative_control: HELD. The same program with PG_NEGATIVE_CONTROL, which replaces the one invalid access with a valid one, completes on this arm with no fault (results/20261010-control). The detection therefore depends on the defect and not on the allocation pattern.

poisoncap-spatial.oracle: complete, with one tolerated double release; the adapter's active[] table counts it as tolerated_double_drops rather than refusing, so the unprotected arm is genuinely unprotected

poisoncap-protected.oracle: SIGPROT inside GetMemoryChunkMethodID -- the manager faults reading the revoked chunk's header, before any bookkeeping runs, so there is no read probe to land on

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes with no capability fault; the case's own PG_DEFECT probe prints twice, so the defective sequence provably executed -- REACHED-SILENT (2026-10-05, plain purecap, revocation=1 every_free=0). A use-after-free between two palloc chunks never crosses a malloc boundary, so there is nothing for a malloc-granular revoker to reclaim.
cheribsd-revocation.run: 2026-10-05, CheriBSD riscv64-purecap, built via PG_CORPUS_DIR through ports/postgres/memory-contexts with PG_POISONCAP off

status: poisoncap-spatial and poisoncap-protected run 2026-09-20 under QEMU: mode 0 completes with tolerated_double_drops=1 and mode 1 faults in GetMemoryChunkMethodID, so the pair holds. The Capstone spatial/sublet arms have NOT been run since the corpus was split into one program per case.
nested_why: The object comes from PostgreSQL's own memory manager -- a chunk aset.c or slab.c carved out of a block it took from malloc -- so the defect is nested by the allocator that served it.
